text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Thursday its board of directors decided to suspend payment of a previously announced dividend of $0.075 a share.
The previously announced dividend had a record date of February 17 and a payment date of March 3.
Mercury also said it was unable to refinance an aggregate of $61 million in matured commercial paper through February 5. Another $127 million comes due between now and February 14.
The company said it is in violation of its loan covenants.
Mercury also said it continued to pursue financing.
"We are currently in serious discussion with lenders with regard to a short-term financing package," William Brandt Jr., president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
He said it is expected that the funds from the short term financing will be used exclusively for operating purposes and will not be available for paying principal or interest on company debt.

Salomon Brothers, engaged by Mercury last week to advise on financial matters, continues to work to arrange a long term financing package, as well as to examine all capital raising alternatives in the course of its review.
Operations continue at all of the company's 280 locations nationwide.
